The prophet Samuel gave the people a long laundry list of what would happen if they had a king – none of it was positive. The king will take away your sons and daughters and put them into servitude. He will take some of your land and animals, j ust to name a few of the points.

They had clear warning of the results of having a king like everyone else!

1 Samuel 8:19-20: (NASB) 19Nevert heless, t he people refused t o list en t o t he voice of Samuel, and t hey said, No, but t here shall be a king over us, 20t hat we also may be like all t he nat ions, t hat our king may j udge us and go out before us and fight our bat t les.

Who was it who led their battles up to this point? (God!) They wanted a king to deliver them in battle instead of God Almighty?

Being God’ s chosen people does not mean sin and self-will goes away.

They were given choices to stay in the blessings of God or face the consequences of poor choices. The people were warned and they suffered mightily under these desired kings.

God let them have kings. They got what they asked for, for generations and generations.

Idolatry – putting something else before God - seemed to ALWAYS be a problem for Israel.

Another choice came in the time of Elijah when Ahab and the prophets of Baal faced Elijah:

1 Kings 18:21-22: (NASB) 21Elij ah came near t o all t he people and said, how long will you hesit at e bet ween t wo opinions? If t he LORD is God, follow Him; but if Baal, follow him. But t he people did not answer him a word. 22Then Elij ah said t o t he people, I alone am left a prophet of t he LORD, but Baal's prophet s are 450 men.

It was 850 to 1, including the 400 prophets of Asherah!

Elij ah set up the challenge of having fire from heaven consume the sacrifice to show the true God. Elij ah had the prophets go first and then would take his turn. Of course, God heard Elij ah’ s prayer.

Remember, these are the chosen people of God worshipping other gods! God made that promise to Abraham, but Israel had problems being faithful throughout most generations. God still did not abandon them.

The prophets were yelling, screaming and cutting themselves, with their blood going on the altars. Elij ah taunted them by suggesting Baal must be sleeping, or maybe he was on a trip.

Then it was Elijah’s turn:

1 Kings 18:39: (NASB) When all t he people saw it , t hey fell on t heir faces; and t hey said, The LORD, He is God; t he LORD, He is God.

Not only was the sacrifice consumed, as was the challenge, but so was everything around it - the wood, stone, water and dirt were all consumed by the fire!

With so much drama, one would think they would never stray again! But that is not human nature.

Sometimes, in spite of the people’ s lack of faith, God delivered them due to the faith and obedience of an individual.

Here was Elij ah standing up for the people, and because of him, God continued giving hope and opportunity.

Like Elij ah, in our Christian walk, we share the same choice: Listen to God's word, or listen to the noise coming from all different directions. Our loyalty is being tested.

Israel ran hot and cold with their obedience, but God never changed His promise. A promise from God is j ust a fact that has not yet been discovered.

Israel’ s choices continued in the New Testament. John the Baptist directly pointed to Jesus as their Messiah, and therefore provoked yet another choice.

The priests and Levites were sent to question John the Baptist to find out who he was:

John 1:24-27,29-30: (NASB) 24Now t hey had been sent from t he Pharisees. 25They asked him, and said t o him, Why t hen are you bapt izing, if you are not t he Christ , nor Elij ah, nor t he Prophet ? 26John answered t hem saying, I bapt ize in wat er, but among you st ands one whom you do not know. 27It is he who comes aft er me, t he t hong of whose sandal I am not wort hy t o unt ie. 29The next day he saw Jesus coming t o him and said, Behold, t he Lamb of God who t akes away t he sin of t he world! 30This is he on behalf of whom I said, aft er me comes a man who has a higher rank t han I, for he exist ed before me.

Are you him, the promised Messiah? No, but the one coming after me is! The next day he saw Jesus coming t o him and said, Behold, t he Lamb of God who t akes away t he sin of t he world! John made it plain, showing the people who their Messiah was.

Many of the average people loved and followed Jesus, but not the rulers:

Matthew 23:37-39: (NASB) 37Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills t he prophet s and st ones t hose who are sent t o her! How oft en I want ed t o gat her your children t oget her, t he way a hen gat hers her chicks under her wings, and you were unwilling. 38Behold, your house is being left t o you desolat e! 39For I say t o you, from now on you will not see me unt il you say, blessed is he who comes in t he name of t he Lord!

The nation was rej ected and desolation soon would follow. But there is a hint of a promise of the future because God makes a promise and it stays intact. To the Pharisees, and therefore to Israel as a nation, Jesus warned, your house is left desolat e. This was a dramatic statement of disfavor, but with a small thread of hope of a future blessing, even though it was small compared to the national desolation that followed.

History can always help us understand the present and even see into the future, but only if we perceive it in the context of God’ s plan.

Does Jesus having cast off Israel from God’s favor bury them as a nation? Does Israel have any hope at all?

The answer to this question is a resounding, emphatic, unequivocal, undeniable YES! While we see Israel’ s disfavor as a tragic result of choosing darkness over light, we know Jesus himself showed us the hope that they would have. Why have hope after such a rej ection? Because this was all in the capable hands of God’ s plans and purposes. God had promised, and He would deliver!

Jesus himself prophesied that Israel would be cut off:

Luke 13:6-9: (NASB) 6And he began t elling t his parable: a man had a fig t ree which had been plant ed in his vineyard; and he came looking for fruit on it and did not find any. 7And he said t o t he vineyard-keeper, Behold, for t hree years I have come looking for fruit on t his fig t ree wit hout finding any.

Cut it down! Why does it even use up t he ground? 8And he answered and said t o him, Let it alone, sir, for t his year t oo, unt il I dig around it and put in fert ilizer; 9and if it bears fruit next year, fine; but if not , cut it down.

This is a dramatic pict ure of Israel being on trial and not “ bearing fruit” for the three years of Jesus’ ministry. There were six months left of Jesus’ ministry before God would begin casting Israel off. This parable was told about a week before his crucifixion.

After riding into Jerusalem and cleansing the Temple, Jesus shows what is about to happen through his treatment of a fig tree:

Matthew 21:18-19: (NASB) 18Now in t he morning, when he was ret urning t o t he cit y, he became hungry. 19Seeing a lone fig t ree by t he road, he came t o it and found not hing on it except leaves only; and he said t o it , No longer shall t here ever be any fruit from you. And at once t he fig t ree wit hered.

Jesus will also use that same symbol of the fig tree to show Israel’ s hope. The symbol of the fig tree shows the problem with Israel, its hope and the fulfillment of promise.

The fig tree withered because Jesus knew what was coming.

Jesus’ actions were a result of what he saw and what he knew was prophesied long before he said the words that caused the tree to wither:

Jeremiah 16:9: (NASB) For t hus says t he LORD of host s, t he God of Israel: Behold, I am going t o eliminat e from t his place, before your eyes and in your t ime, t he voice of rej oicing and t he voice of gladness, t he voice of t he groom and t he voice of t he bride.

I am going t o eliminat e…t he voice of rej oicing and t he voice of gladness, t he voice of t he groom and t he voice of t he bride. This is sad. Joy is taken away. The prophecy continues to say, the people will demand an explanation for such harsh treatment:

Jeremiah 16:11-13: (NASB) 11Then you are t o say t o t hem, It is because your forefat hers have forsaken Me, declares t he LORD, and have followed ot her gods and served t hem and bowed down t o t hem;…12You t oo have done evil, even more t han your forefat hers; for behold, you are each one walking according t o t he st ubbornness of his own evil heart , wit hout list ening t o Me.

13So I will hurl you out of t his land int o t he land which you have not known, neit her you nor your fat hers; and t here you will serve ot her gods day and night , for I will grant you no favor. Putting this into context with the Amos 3:1-2 texts we read earlier, it is harsh and sad. They are demanding an explanation of what is happening. The explanation is that their forefathers were bad. They did not stay faithful. There is a pause, and then he says, “ Wait! You were even worse!”

The reason they were worse is because they had the Messiah in front of them. They saw his miracles, they heard his teaching, they observed his character through his life, they saw his perfect example, and yet they rej ected him. I will hurl you out of t his land – this is such a dramatic sadness for Israel, the Jewish nation, God’ s chosen people.

While it is heartbreaking, it was a necessary heartbreak because God’ s promises are bigger than the moment . We must never forget that.

His warning to them was his last public statement before he died, as he spoke this warning while carrying his cross to Calvary:

Luke 23:28-30: (NASB) 28But Jesus t urning t o t hem said, Daught ers of Jerusalem, st op weeping for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children. 29For behold, t he days are coming when t hey will say, Blessed are t he barren, and t he wombs t hat never bore, and t he breast s t hat never nursed. 30Then t hey will begin t o say t o t he mount ains, fall on us, and t o t he hills, cover us.

This was the last public statement of Jesus: Weep f or yourselves and f or your children - how could he have given a statement while carrying his cross in agony? His focus was on what was happening to natural Israel. “ This is what is coming because you rej ected me as your Messiah.”

It is hard to imagine not weeping while watching this man who has been beaten to a pulp, now carrying this cross, because it is the most tragic, sad thing. He stops as he is carrying his cross with all these people around watching. He makes this public proclamation that they are to weep for themselves – that what they are observing is the beginning of something that will be tragic for them.

This gives us a sense of his character, the insight, focus, clarity and especially the determination of Jesus even hours before his death. It is remarkable. This sounds like a path from which there is no return; we are not building up a good case for the promise to be fulfilled, but this isn’ t the end of the story! We paused where Jeremiah is quoting God saying, I will hurl you out of t his land.

Let’s read on:

Jeremiah 16:14-15: (NASB) 14Therefore behold, days are coming, declares t he LORD, when it will no longer be said, as t he LORD lives, who brought up t he sons of Israel out of t he land of Egypt , 15but , as t he LORD lives, who brought up t he sons of Israel from t he land of t he nort h and from all t he count ries where He had banished t hem. For I will rest ore t hem t o t heir own land which I gave t o t heir fat hers.

This statement is far more dramatic than we may realize. The entire Bible uses the deliverance of Israel from the bondage of Egyptian slavery as a marker of the absolute greatness of God and His power. This deliverance will be recognized as exponentially larger than that from Egypt!

This regathering of Israel started in 1878, 70 years before they became a nation again in 1948. And 70 years later, Jerusalem was recognized as the capital of Israel.

This shows us an unfolding process. We cannot deny that Israel is an actual nation in the world. They were not a nation for all those preceding generations before Jesus. How did that happen? This is God’ s promise beginning to show itself as a guaranteed fact that others did not see happening yet.

It will no longer be said, as t he LORD lives, who brought up t he sons of Israel out of t he land of Egypt . Remember, the phrase, Brought you out of t he land of Egypt appears over 80 times in the Bible. One of the big markers of all of Scripture is the delivering of Israel out of the land of Egypt, out of slavery. But these Jeremiah 16 scriptures tell us that Egyptian deliverance was a small sampling of what THIS deliverance is going to accomplish. This is God’ s promise. We will see something bigger.

The prophecy continues with harsh sayings about the sending of fishers and hunters that bring Israel back home. But THEN:

Jeremiah 16:17-18: (NASB) 17For My eyes are on all t heir ways; t hey are not hidden from My face, nor is t heir iniquit y concealed from My eyes. 18I will first doubly repay t heir iniquit y and t heir sin, because t hey have pollut ed My land; t hey have filled My inherit ance wit h t he carcasses of t heir det est able idols and wit h t heir abominat ions.

In other words: “ I know how bad they are, and yet, My deliverance for them this time will be the marker that unfolds the door to eternity.”

This marker is Israel being regathered from the four corners of the world. We are actually seeing that piece of prophecy in play right this very minute. What most of us do not realize is that it is the beginning of the marker that shows God’ s eternal plan. This is how big it is! It is bigger than deliverance from Egyptian slavery mentioned many times in the Bible.

And yet that deliverance is nothing compared to this.

The Apostle Paul knew of - and looked forward to - the restoring of Israel to godly favor before the disfavor really took effect:

Romans 11:11-12: (NASB) 11I say t hen, t hey did not st umble so as t o fall, did t hey? May it never be! But by t heir t ransgression salvat ion has come t o t he Gent iles, t o make t hem j ealous. 12Now if t heir t ransgression is riches for t he world and t heir failure is riches for t he Gent iles, how much more will t heir fulfillment be!

Paul knew Israel would be restored. He understood the faithfulness of a promise of God. However, because of the failure of Israel, the call to discipleship to Christ went out to the Gentile nations. Without Israel’ s failure, few Gentiles would have become Christians. There is a tremendous blessing to many as a result of Israel’ s failure.

This shows us consequences for wrong actions, and also shows us blessings for godly obedience. All things in time as God unfolds His plan:

Romans 11:15: (NASB) For if t heir rej ect ion is t he reconciliat ion of t he world, what will t heir accept ance be but life from t he dead?

We must j ust pause and read scriptures like this slowly to let ourselves absorb what is being said about the physical nation of Israel.

Soon, the regathering and restoring of Israel back to full favor with God will be recognized as one of the most powerful proofs of God’ s power and plan throughout all the world, according to prophecy.

This is the key to God’ s plan. He allows sin and degradation so the experience can give us the clarity to know we never want to go back there. Mankind will have had enough and will want to move on to something bigger and better. As we see these things being put in order, it is hard to wrap our minds around the depth, forethought and power of God’ s plan!

When does this amazing regathering take place?

What will be the end result of God’s chosen people being fully restored? The short answer to these questions was revealed right when we began. God’ s promise to Abraham explicitly and repeat edly described the blessings of all the families of the earth. While we know this blessing comes from Jesus as THE “ seed of blessing,” we will also see many prophecies unmistakably show us the physical nation of Israel will play a maj or role in this blessing as well. Many Christians think the nation of Israel is no longer a part of God’ s plan. They believe “ spiritual Israel” (Christians) is the replacement for the physical nation of Israel. But the prophecies and scriptures show us God’ s plan is bigger than that. God gave a promise; He verified the physical part of His plan as well as the spiritual part. One part doesn’ t replace the other; the two parts will work together in perfect harmony because that is God’ s promise.

When Jesus prophesied the signs of his return, he quietly told us Israel’s regathering and beginning stages of favor would be one of those signs:

Luke 21:29-31: (NASB) 29Then he t old t hem a parable: Behold t he fig t ree and all t he t rees; 30as soon as t hey put fort h leaves, you see it and know for yourselves t hat summer is now near. 31So you also, when you see t hese t hings happening, recognize t hat t he kingdom of God is near. This began in 1878 in the town called Petah Tikva, which means “ Doorway of Hope.” Petah Tikva was a fulfillment of prophecy.

God is eternal. His promises may not come to fruition for thousands of years after humanity has lost sight of them. But when the time comes for a promise to be fulfilled, the fulfillment is unmistakable.

In Luke 21:29-31, Jesus is talking about his return. He is saying that his return is tied to the restoration of Israel. This is a big hint as to how God’ s plan is unfolding.

The Apostle Paul sets us on a path of prophecy as he continues describing Israel’s regathering and restoration:

Romans 11:25-27: (NASB) 25For I do not want you, bret hren, t o be uninformed of t his myst ery—so t hat you will not be wise in your own est imat ion—t hat a part ial hardening has happened t o Israel unt il t he fullness of t he Gent iles has come in; 26and so all Israel will be saved; j ust as it is writ t en, t he deliverer will come from Zion, he will remove ungodliness from Jacob. 27This is my covenant wit h t hem, when I t ake away t heir sins.

Paul, the apostle to the Gentiles, is talking about the physical nation of Israel. Is the Jewish nation really God’ s chosen people? The answer is unequivocally YES. All Israel will be saved…when I t ake away t heir sins.

When we tie Scripture together, we see a harmonious message. Paul is quoting an Old Testament prophecy. Some Christians look at these prophecies and believe a limited application was only to the Jews of that time. But because Paul brings it forward to the time of the New Testament, we know it applies to both the Jews in the Old Testament and to the future.

Paul quotes from Isaiah, so we know this prophecy has a future fulfillment:

Isaiah 59:20-21: (NASB) 20A redeemer will come t o Zion, and t o t hose who t urn from t ransgression in Jacob, declares t he LORD. 21As for Me, t his is My covenant wit h t hem, says t he LORD: My spirit which is upon you, and My words which I have put in your mout h shall not depart from your mout h, nor from t he mout h of your offspring, nor from t he mout h of your offspring's offspring, says t he LORD, from now and forever.

But didn’t Jesus come to Zion 2,000 years ago? But none of this came true at that time.

This is why he returns. Jesus’ return accomplishes this, as Israel rej ected him at his first advent. How do we know this? Because God promised it, and the return of Jesus is proof of His promise.

There are many reasons why Jesus returns: to gather the true saints to heaven, to tear down the kingdoms (governments and societies) of this earth and to fully restore the nation of Israel. There will be a New Covenant established with Israel, spoken of in Jeremiah.

Jeremiah further helps us to see the power of this New Covenant with Israel:

Jeremiah 31:31-34: (NASB) 31Behold, days are coming, declares t he LORD, when I will make a new covenant wit h t he house of Israel and wit h t he house of Judah, 32not like t he covenant which I made wit h t heir fat hers in t he day I t ook t hem by t he hand t o bring t hem out of t he land of Egypt , My covenant which t hey broke, alt hough I was a husband t o t hem, declares t he LORD.

The Old (Law) Covenant came as a result of Israel’ s deliverance from Egypt. The New Covenant comes as a result of Israel’s deliverance from being scattered throughout the world and nearly destroyed: 33But t his is t he covenant which I will make wit h t he house of Israel aft er t hose days, declares t he LORD, I will put My law wit hin t hem and on t heir heart I will writ e it ; and I will be t heir God, and t hey shall be My people.

How beautiful it is that the Old Law Covenant was written on stone tablets, but the New Covenant will be written on their hearts. 34They will not t each again, each man his neighbor and each man his brot her, saying, know t he LORD, for t hey will all know Me, from t he least of t hem t o t he great est of t hem, declares t he LORD, for I will forgive t heir iniquit y, and t heir sin I will remember no more. This compares the Old Covenant and the New Covenant. The New Covenant will be different, more comprehensive and written on the hearts of the people. It will not be imposed on them from the outside; instead, they will have an inside, heart understanding of God.

We see t he incredible depth of God’ s promises. This is not about a theoretical nation full of theoretical people at some theoretical time. This is about real human beings having this covenant written on their hearts, one at a time. How beautiful!

How long will this new favor and this New Covenant last? Jeremiah described it:

Jeremiah 31:35-36: (NASB) 35Thus says t he LORD, Who gives t he sun for light by day and t he fixed order of t he moon and t he st ars for light by night , who st irs up t he sea so t hat it s waves roar; The LORD of host s is His name: 36If t his fixed order depart s from before Me, declares t he LORD, t hen t he offspring of Israel also will cease from being a nat ion before Me forever. This is an earthly prophecy for an earthly nation. Some Christians believe the physical earth will be burned up, but this prophecy disproves that thought.

It is saying as long as the fixed order of God’ s creation is intact, His promises will endure. We are looking into eternity when we read this prophecy. …in your seed all t he nat ions of t he eart h shall be blessed – t he magnit ude of this promise is eternity!

What will this eternal covenant with Israel accomplish for the rest of resurrected humanity?

Micah 4:1-4: (NASB) 1And it will come about in t he last days t hat t he mount ain of t he house of t he LORD (God’ s government) will be est ablished as t he chief of t he mount ains.

It will be raised above t he hills, and t he peoples will st ream t o it . 2Many nat ions will come and say, Come and let us go up t o t he mount ain of t he LORD and t o t he house of t he God of Jacob (Israel), t hat He may t each us about His ways and t hat we may walk in His pat hs. For from Zion will go fort h t he law, even t he word of t he LORD from Jerusalem. All will be educated based on the truth. All the nations will be flocking to the God of Israel to learn God’ s laws coming from Jerusalem, the capital of the world in the future kingdom.

God made a little, short promise to Abraham thousands of years ago. We see it magnified and dramatized throughout the Bible. 3And He will j udge bet ween many peoples and render decisions for might y, dist ant nat ions... Judgment will be part of this. The Day of Judgment is a time of reconciliation and reckoning, a time of growing into the righteousness of God through Christ, as shown by Israel. ...Then (as a result) t hey will hammer t heir swords int o plowshares and t heir spears int o pruning hooks; nat ion will not lift up sword against nat ion, and never again will t hey t rain for war. 4Each of t hem will sit under his vine and under his fig t ree, wit h no one t o make t hem afraid, for t he mout h of t he LORD of host s has spoken.

After God’ s government is put in place, there will be no more war. World peace at last! The mout h of t he LORD of host s has spoken - when God makes a promise, NOTHING can change it.

John 15:5: (NASB) I am the vine, you are the branches; he who abides in me and I in him, he bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.

So, is the Jewish nation really God’s chosen people?

## Episode 1232 — Is the Gospel Obsolete?
Published: 2022-06-06
Episode page: https://christianquestions.com/doctrine/1232-gospel-obsolete/

Romans 10:15: (NASB) How will they preach unless they are sent?

Just as it is written, how beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news of good things!

We live in an age of tremendous knowledge, phenomenal technology and unprecedented freedom. On one hand, ours is an age where the individual reigns supreme. I can decide what is right and wrong for me, and I can also expect others to make allowances for my conclusions. On the other hand, the Gospel of Jesus Christ tells us right from wrong and moral from immoral.

It defines our treatment of others, how to live and why we should live that way. The gospel is all about calling out a people for God’s name through Jesus and proclaiming that God’s kingdom is in fact coming! With the way this world operates, does this gospel message and its way of life even matter? Are the personal freedoms of our present social order beyond the reach of the gospel?

We begin with some of Jesus’ final words to his disciples:

Matthew 28:16-20: (NASB) 16But the eleven disciples proceeded to Galilee, to the mountain which Jesus had designated. 17When they saw him, they worshiped him; but some were doubtful. 18And Jesus came up and spoke to them, saying, all authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth. 19Go therefore and make disciples <3100> of all the nations <1484>, baptizing them in the name of the Father and the son and the holy spirit, 20teaching them to observe all that I commanded you; and lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.

Disciples: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance #3100; matheteuo; to become a pupil; transitively, to disciple, i.e. enroll as scholar Jesus is looking for thoroughly committed individuals for his cause. He is not looking for fans who cheer for him. The calling of individuals is much more than a “Jesus Fan Club.” It is about enrolling as scholars, to learn how to follow in his path the best way we know how.

Nations: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance #1484; ethnos; a race (as of the same habit), i.e. a tribe; specially, a foreign (non-Jewish) one (usually by implication, pagan)

The King James Version translates this as Gentile, heathen, nation and people Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations - the idea is to make disciples (scholars, true followers) from all different nations. It does not matter where they come from, but they should all follow in the footsteps of Jesus.

Jesus spoke these words just before his ascension:

Luke 24:46-49: (NASB) 46and he said to them, Thus it is written, that the Christ would suffer and rise again from the dead the third day, 47and that repentance for forgiveness of sins would be proclaimed <2784> in his name to all the nations, beginning from Jerusalem. 48You are witnesses of these things. 49And behold, I am sending forth the promise of my Father upon you; but you are to stay in the city until you are clothed with power from on high.

Proclaimed: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance #2784 kerusso; of uncertain affinity; to herald (as a public crier), especially divine truth (the gospel) It is not about converting; it is about proclaiming the good news. This is an important distinction. Jesus is saying proclaim, speak it out, give people hope, let them know this is about the kingdom, this is about my sacrifice – LET THEM KNOW! Everybody will not respond, but that is okay.

1. (Luke) Jesus would send God’s spirit to guide the disciples in all they were being required to do.

2. (Luke) The disciples were to preach/proclaim repentance and the remission of sins everywhere they went, in all nations.

3. (Matthew) Make disciples out of all nations, but start at home in Jerusalem.

4. (Luke) Baptize in the name of the Father, son and holy spirit.

Baptism symbolizes the disciple’s source of life (the Father), the source of redemption (the son) and the source of their enlightenment (the holy spirit).

5. (Matthew) Teach the words and commands of Jesus to these new followers, exactly as the disciples themselves learned them.

The Apostle Paul reiterates this responsibility of the gospel message:

Romans 10:14-15: (NASB) 14How then will they call on him in whom they have not believed?

How will they believe in him whom they have not heard? And how will they hear without a preacher? 15How will they preach unless they are sent? Just as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news of good things! (as quoted from Isaiah 52:7) The gospel does not preach itself; it needs representation. It needs disciples preaching the message.

The obvious mission here is to preach the gospel to the world. The not-so- obvious mission is that this preaching - while bringing disciples - will not convert the world.

In our day, we, as followers of Jesus, are bringing a message the world really does not like. Hence our question, Is the gospel obsolete?

When we look around at what goes on in the world, what people are talking about and what attracts them, the gospel is rarely a part of it. We have to ask, what are we doing? It seems like preaching the gospel will fall continuously on deaf ears. Should we just accept that?

Let’s pause on the mission of the gospel and review just a few of the many ways the gospel personally transforms us.

John 13:14: (NASB) If I then, the Lord and the Teacher, washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet.

This is a simple, straightforward lesson of serving one another. No matter how humble the service is, just do it! This is what Jesus did. Remember, being a disciple is like being a scholar or student. We have to learn in a scholarly way how to wash one another’s feet, how to have the attitude of love and servitude.

John 15:12: (NASB) this is my commandment, that you love one another, just as I have loved you.

This love is agape in Greek, meaning the selfless, benevolent love we often talk about.

This is my commandment - Jesus is not just making a suggestion. We are to learn to love one another in a selfless way. What a responsibility!

Luke 9:23: (NASB) And he was saying to them all, If anyone wishes to come after me, he must deny himself, and take up his cross daily and follow me.

We first talked about what we are supposed to DO with the gospel. Now we see what we are supposed to BE. The gospel transforms us so that we can bring this message of transformation to others.

In summary, the gospel contains the words, teachings and example of Jesus, as exemplified not only in the books of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John, but also the rest of the New Testament.

The gospel message is GOOD NEWS of hope to all.

While the general population is too preoccupied with their own issues to pay attention or even care, eternal hope and righteousness are ALWAYS relevant.

Eternal hope and eternal righteousness, no matter what the circumstance, has relevance. Eternal outcomes are much more powerful than that which is transitory. We have to see the gospel as relevant, even if it does not always seem to fit our needs. It has a distinct purpose.

The gospel is a BIG message about a BIG plan that will bring BIG changes. The beauty is, everyone will benefit.

So, the gospel message is relevant.

What are some of the primary building blocks to make the gospel our own? Having the gospel message preached to us and applying its value on a personal level are two very different things. We will begin to examine just three of the potentially life-changing primary building blocks of the gospel. We will find these building blocks are simple and sound life principles.

Our first primary building block of the gospel is HUMILITY - plain, simple, genuine humility. It is a simple concept but hard to manage. We constantly fail.

Jesus is and always will be the primary example of what the gospel teaches us about humility:

Philippians 2:6-9: (NASB) 6who, although he existed in the form of God, did not regard equality with God a thing to be grasped, 7but emptied himself, taking the form of a bond- servant, and being made in the likeness of men. 8Being found in appearance as a man, he humbled himself by becoming obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross. 9For this reason also, God highly exalted him, and bestowed on him the name which is above every name. God had Jesus with Him, as Jesus was the first and primary creation of God.

Jesus emptied himself of that high and lofty spiritual position. He was willing to be completely emptied of it to become a human. After becoming a man, he emptied himself of his humanity by being willing to die for the purpose of doing God’s just and righteous will. Jesus emptied himself twice! We are only expected to do it once. Jesus did it twice from a perspective we cannot even fathom. That is why for this reason also, God highly exalted him, and bestowed on him the name which is above every name. It shows us the grandeur of what his humility produced.

Is this kind of humility common in our world or is it obsolete? This kind of humility is hard to find, but this is our example. It cannot be obsolete for us, because we are supposed to strive for it.

For us to aspire to the humility of Jesus, we need to be focused on others. Why?

Think of the actions of Jesus in light of this prophetic description of him:

Isaiah 6:8-10: (NIV) 8Then I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then I said, Here am I. Send me! 9He (God) said, Be ever hearing, but never understanding; be ever seeing, but never perceiving. 10Make the heart of this people calloused; make their ears dull and close their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn and be healed.

Jesus was sent to preach the good news which would only be received by those being specifically called by God. The followers of Jesus have the same mission, and the message most likely will not be received by very many. This is why Jesus quoted this prophecy from Isaiah 6 when he preached the Parable of the Sower and the Seed in Matthew 13:1-23.

Luke 8:10: (NASB) And he said, To you it has been granted to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God, but to the rest it is in parables, so that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.

God sent Jesus, knowing this would happen. Therefore, when we preach the gospel, we do not count “success” as how many people respond to the message. Instead, we are supposed to look at the proclamation, effort, humility and the giving of the good news. It is exactly that – good news - but it must be approached with genuine humility.

We need to aspire to genuine humility:

Galatians 6:1-2: (NASB) 1Brethren, even if anyone is caught in any trespass, you who are spiritual, restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness; each one looking to yourself, so that you too will not be tempted. 2Bear one another's burdens, and thereby fulfill the law of Christ. These are such beautiful texts showing us how to fulfill the law of Christ!

The gospel requires humility from us. To wholeheartedly bear another’s burdens requires selfless love as expressed through empathy.

Let’s define empathy: The first of the two parts of empathy, Narcissism, Dr. Ramani - First of all, it's important to understand empathy has two pieces: It's the piece of attempting to understand, reflect and be present with the emotions or feelings of another person. Even if you're not experiencing them, and perhaps even if you don't necessarily agree with them, that you would understand that a person may be sad or angry or have some other emotional state.

Empathy is a powerful word that we do not use enough. For me, it is three basic things: First, it is learning to be quiet enough to understand what somebody is telling us. We often think we understand and want to finish the sentence, but instead we need to be quiet enough to really hear what they are saying.

Second, be absolutely, sincerely interested in what they are saying. That means we’ve cut out all other distractions. We put down what we were doing, turning away from the things that are going to draw our attention, and focus in on that person.

Third, I have had the wonderful privilege of learning about things that have happened to people that have not happened to me. I can’t sympathize with those things because I don’t know what it feels like. But in empathy, I can walk by their side as they attempt to deal with it.

So, if we are quiet enough and sincerely interested, we can then walk with them. To me, that’s what empathy is. It is transformative.

To be empathetic requires a humility to give space so that others can occupy our hearts.

Does our world value empathy? It depends. When tragedy strikes the way it has in our recent school shootings here in the United States, we would have to say, of course the world has empathy. But in the political climate, there is very little empathy for each other’s viewpoint. Many just want to throw poisonous darts at the opposition. Since our society is so selfish in general, there is very little deep empathy. But there are many good people in this world.

The world can be empathetic, but it is focused during specific times and for specific reasons. It is true, we generally see great empathy during tragedy. While we are able to give people space in our hearts, we do not seem to be able to keep them there. This basic humility is scarcely taught in our world, but it does exist. We can see it during those tragic times when everybody just stops and feels. This is an important way to begin a healing process. But the value of empathy is deeper than an occasional happening.

Its value is powerfully described in the Bible:

James 4:5-8: (NASB) 5Or do you think that the scripture speaks to no purpose (here he quotes the scripture): He jealously desires the spirit which He has made to dwell in us? 6But He gives a greater grace. Therefore it says, God is opposed to the proud (conspicuous, haughty), but gives grace to the humble. 7Submit therefore to God. Resist the devil and he will flee from you. 8Draw near to God and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners; and purify your hearts, you double-minded.

For us to grab hold of empathy, we need to first be humble. Humility requires submission to righteous things and the resisting of evil. “NO! Evil will not live here!” Humility requires drawing near to the good that God has presented to us and cleansing ourselves.

Once we have put this process in order, we can then focus on the second part of empathy. Remember, the first part was being quiet, observing and entering into someone else’s experiences. Let them affect us, accepting what the other person is feeling even if we do not feel the same.

The second part of empathy is what we do next, and here is where most of us drop the ball: The second of the two parts of empathy, Narcissism, Dr. Ramani - But part two of empathy is being able to self-reflect on your impact on other people. So, in the simplest example, empathy - the self-part of empathy, the self-reflective part of empathy - is taking a minute before you react to someone, to think about how your words and how your actions could affect somebody else.

Often we quietly listened and appreciated their feelings, but now we need to think about our reaction. We need to evaluate what our reaction will do for them or against them. Am I going to be helpful? I have been empathetic, but will my response relay something positive, or will it end up negative? This self-reflection requires internal thinking and observation. This is not easy or common. Narcissism, which seems to be a growing problem today, rebels against this self-reflection.

(Source: https://www.webmd.com/mental-health/narcissism-symptoms-signs) Narcissism is extreme self-involvement to the degree that it makes a person ignore the needs of those around them. While everyone may show occasional narcissistic behavior, true narcissists frequently disregard others or their feelings. They also do not understand the effect that their behavior has on other people.

Signs of Narcissism: Sense of Entitlement, Manipulative Behavior, Need for Admiration, Arrogance, Lack of Empathy.

Lack of empathy is another sign of narcissism. This means that the narcissist is unwilling or unable to empathize with the needs, wants, or feelings of other people. This also makes it difficult for them to take responsibility for their own behavior.

If somebody is narcissistic, they are so absorbed with themselves that they have a hard time applying empathy in a positive way. This is not to say they cannot ever be empathetic. We will go into that later.

While we are not at all suggesting that everyone in the world is a diagnosable narcissist, we are suggesting that narcissistic tendencies are overwhelmingly prevalent in our social media society.

Social media is about me presenting me to you. It is really all about ME. This narcissistic attitude and self-absorption overtakes us and skews our view of everything else.

The symptoms of this narcissistic approach are not new, and they are not unique to the present:

Romans 1:21-25: (NASB) 21For even though they knew God, they did not honor Him as God or give thanks, but they became futile in their speculations, and their foolish heart was darkened. 22Professing to be wise, they became fools, 23and exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for an image in the form of corruptible man and of birds and four-footed animals and crawling creatures. 24Therefore God gave them over in the lusts of their hearts to impurity, so that their bodies would be dishonored among them. 25For they exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.

This is pure and simple idolatry, putting the created before the Creator and saying, I’m the most important thing!

This takes us away from empathy.

This is why the gospel does not fit in this world. But, is it obsolete? No!

We need to be able to rise above what is all around us.

Leadership tends to invite personal pride to well up and distort that which is sacred to become that which is arrogant.

Without true humility, whatever empathy we have is going to go awry:

1 Peter 5:1-3: (NASB) 1Therefore, I exhort the elders among you, as your fellow elder…

Peter could have said: I'm the one who brought the gospel to you, or, I'm the one who gave that great sermon at Pentecost. But no; he is simply saying: I am a fellow elder. This is humility! …and witness of the sufferings of Christ, and a partaker also of the glory that is to be revealed, 2shepherd the flock of God among you, exercising oversight not under compulsion, but voluntarily, according to the will of God; and not for sordid gain, but with eagerness; 3nor yet as lording it over those allotted to your charge, but proving to be examples to the flock. Peter was saying to eagerly give of ourselves (shepherd the flock) because we want to, with no thought of getting anything in return. This is what good leadership should look like. Empathy is easier with this kind of an attitude. Peter, of all men, was well-qualified to teach the early church leaders humility, as he had to learn it himself.

For leadership to be effective and transformative, the leader must have their fingers upon their OWN pulse with just as much intensity as they have them on the pulse of those they lead:

1 Peter 5:4-7: (NASB) 4And when the Chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the unfading crown of glory. 5You younger men, likewise, be subject to your elders; and all of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, for God is opposed to the proud (haughty), But gives grace to the humble. 6Therefore humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, that He may exalt you at the proper time, 7casting all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you. We cannot say to God, “I did a good deed today! Did You see that? I need to be recognized!”

Humble Christians rely on God to lift them up in an appropriate and God- honoring way. If it is not an appropriate time, then we still rejoice that we were able to serve humbly and without fanfare.

The gospel requires humility in those who will follow its message. More often than not, our world encourages a brash and arrogant attitude in those who will follow its causes. As our social discourse becomes ever more toxic, we can see that empathy - true humility-driven empathy - is blatantly absent.

The humility of the gospel IS relevant!

The gospel is not obsolete, but it IS uncomfortable to the world.

If we injure our knee and have to wear a brace, it often hurts. But it is supporting the knee so that it can heal. Even though it chafes and hurts, that brace is necessary. The relevance of the gospel is that in order to heal, the world needs this example set, this chiding reminder, even though the world does not want or like the example.

Humility-driven empathy seems so simple and yet is hard to apply because it requires ME to let go of ME!

What effect does a lack of humility and empathy have on our ability to adhere to any kind of moral code?

Defining morality is a massive part of our social media culture. When we look at the relevance of the gospel in our world today, perhaps the most obvious area of divergence is in regard to moral codes. This world is a free-for-all morally, while the gospel comes complete with an intact and detailed moral code.

Round peg/square hole, right? It is not going to fit! But that does not mean we stop working with it.

MORALITY is having a clear-cut code that defines right and wrong.

As messengers of the gospel, Christians are overwhelmingly instructed to follow righteousness as defined by God:

2 Timothy 2:3-5: (NASB) 3Suffer hardship with me, as a good soldier of Christ Jesus. 4No soldier in active service entangles himself in the affairs of everyday life, so that he may please the one who enlisted him as a soldier. 5Also if anyone competes as an athlete, he does not win the prize unless he competes according to the rules.

Such simple, clear statements! We are not supposed to win by cheating. We have to have the same high level of morality the Apostle Paul taught his spiritual son, Timothy. Christians should aim to have Paul’s type of morality and an all-out dedication and belief in Jesus as a model for our daily lives. …unless he competes according to the rules - the rules of the gospel. Not the rules of the gospel as written by us, but as written by Jesus Christ according to the Bible.

As messengers of this gospel, we find empathy to be a key to understanding those around us so as to be able to potentially show them a higher morality and a higher way. If we can apply the two parts of empathy we discussed, we can lift people out of a lower level of morality into the Christian standards of morality.

The positive power of empathy, Narcissism, Dr. Ramani

- Empathy, when used correctly, gives us a lot of information about the other person. It teaches us the sorts of triggers for sadness, the kinds of things that anger them or agitate them, the things that they feel anxious about, and any number of other situations or triggers that bring out strong emotions in a person.

When we put empathy to work, it will teach us about the person we are reaching out to if we pay attention to what they are saying. This is the positive power of empathy. By doing this, we can help them see a higher way, a higher level, a higher morality.

But we then need to look at our world. The other side of the “moral coin” is deciding to make morality fit our own agenda. This is when it is all about ME and what I think is right. Do not judge me.

While we lament at how shockingly far this has gone, it is important to remember that this kind of thinking is not new. It has been repeated throughout history.

We go deeper into darkness every time we repeat history:

Isaiah 5:18-19: (NASB) 18Woe to those who drag iniquity with the cords of falsehood, and sin as if with cart ropes (this is a picture of dragging sin along behind you with ropes: Come along, sin!); 19Who say, Let Him make speed, let Him hasten His work, that we may see it; and let the purpose of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come to pass, that we may know it!

It sounds like they are saying, “Let God show us plainly, and only then we will follow.” This arrogance reminds us of the Pharisees at the cross, mocking

Jesus in Matthew 27:41-42: …let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him.

What audacity they had to say that after all the miracles he had showed them. No matter what evil was thrown at him, Jesus stood his ground. And not only did he stand his ground against evil, while he was hanging there on the cross in such pain, he witnessed to the two thieves on either side of him. While he was dying, he made sure John would take care of his mother. All the while, they were throwing insults at him.

That was his empathy, his high moral code. We can imagine he looked at them and thought: I am dying for you, just like I am dying for those who love me. He understood the power of his sacrifice. We want this same thought process. Isaiah continues, and it gets worse:

Isaiah 5:20-23: (NASB) 20Woe to those who call evil good, and good evil; Who substitute darkness for light and light for darkness; Who substitute bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter!

Isaiah 5:21-23: (NASB) 21Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight! 22Woe to those who are heroes in drinking wine and valiant men in mixing strong drink, 23Who justify the wicked for a bribe, and take away the rights of the ones who are in the right!

We see evil all around us today. How much worse can it get? Is the gospel obsolete? No, but it is certainly out of place being so different from the current worldview. However, we should not ignore it just because it is different. We cannot back away from that which is righteous.

For those who twist and subvert, there is a negative power of empathy as well.

The negative power of empathy, Narcissism Dr. Ramani

- If you study that carefully enough, you better believe that you can then use that knowledge to manipulate that person. If you know what gets a rise out of that person, creates emotions out of them, if you're the narcissist and you're aware - which is empathy - of the other person's emotional state, when you need it you can turn around and use that as a weapon, as a tool, as a way of manipulating them, as a way of getting a rise out of them. And then turning around and gaslighting them and saying, “You're being too sensitive.” This is awful but so easy to do. We can listen and learn enough to turn it against someone. We can use their vulnerability to crush them. This is not how we are supposed to be – our morality should be so much higher than this. Our standard is higher than that of the world around us. Every person is not evil and dark like this – most of us try to be better. But we must be wary and careful against such things. We know this because Christians have these same challenges:

James 1:14-17: (NASB) 14But each one is tempted when he is carried away and enticed by his own lust. 15Then when lust has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and when sin is accomplished, it brings forth death. 16Do not be deceived, my beloved brethren.

New American Standard: when sin is accomplished American Standard Bible: the sin, when it is full-grown Amplified Bible: when sin has run its course 17Every good thing given and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shifting shadow.

James is writing this to Christians saying: We are tempted when we are enticed by our own desire. Doesn’t this sound like those narcissistic tendencies we are talking about? James says to strive to that higher level of morality. Do not be stuck in the way the world deals with things. Stand up for something higher, bigger, stronger, better, wiser, clearer and more compassionate. This is why we need to cling to the gospel in every aspect of our lives. Eventually sin brings death.

God knows the difference between right and wrong, is far above us and has clear objectives in His actions:

Isaiah 55:8-11: (NASB) 8For My thoughts are not your thoughts, nor are your ways My ways, declares the LORD. 9For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are My ways higher than your ways and My thoughts than your thoughts. 10For as the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and do not return there without watering the earth and making it bear and sprout, and furnishing seed to the sower and bread to the eater; 11So will My word be which goes forth from My mouth; it will not return to Me empty, without accomplishing what I desire, and without succeeding in the matter for which I sent it.

God is a God of compassion.

My word…goes forth from My mouth...accomplishing what I desire - we need to believe this and hold onto it - even when we are uncomfortable in this world that does not like what we stand for. It does not mean the gospel is obsolete; it is simply a round peg in a square hole. We are being tested on our example of higher morality and the application of humility and empathy.

God allows man’s immorality for the purpose of teaching us that our own made-up ways are futile.

For those of us who want God’s morality in our lives, we need to see it as the overriding influence in all of our decisions:

Proverbs 16:2: (NASB) All the ways of a man are clean in his own sight, but the LORD weighs the motives.

This reminds us of:

James 4:3: (NASB) You ask and do not receive, because you ask with wrong motives, so that you may spend it on your pleasures.

What are our deep motivations?

Proverbs 16:3-6: 3Commit your works to the LORD and your plans will be established. 4The LORD has made everything for its own purpose, even the wicked for the day of evil. 5Everyone who is proud in heart is an abomination to the LORD; assuredly, he will not be unpunished. Immorality will have consequences! 6By lovingkindness and truth iniquity is atoned for, and by the fear of the LORD one keeps away from evil.

Lovingkindness and truth are who Jesus was, is and will be. We need to adhere to that morality. We do not fit in this world, but it does not matter. It is not that we are obsolete. It is that we are living up to something higher to be an example.

The gospel and its morality are far above that of any morality of human design. Because the vast majority of the world categorically denies God’s morality, it serves as a point of comparison for our broken and selfish ways. This comparison will be used in the future reconciliation of humanity.

The morality we learn from the gospel IS relevant!

The gospel is not obsolete - it is just not comfortable.

Even though morality related to the gospel is presently held in disdain, it is comforting to know its future importance in the work of reconciliation of the world to God.

How does discipleship, our third gospel building block, work together with humility and morality?

We preach the gospel, the good news of the kingdom. In preaching this message, we need to be its humble representatives who live as an example of a higher morality than that with which the world is comfortable. All these are a function of being an actual footstep follower of Jesus, not just a “fan” of him.

Jesus chose to abandon his own will as a man whenever the will of God stood above it:

Psalms 40:7-8: (NASB) 7Then I said, Behold, I come; in the scroll of the book it is written of me. 8I delight to do Your will, O my God; Your Law is within my heart.

This sounds wonderful, and we are excited to do this…until we have to apply it! Then we look at Jesus’ life and the night of his deepest trial and see how he had to apply it:

Matthew 26:39: (NASB) And he went a little beyond them, and fell on his face and prayed, saying, My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me; yet not as I will, but as You will. That is our selfless example. If we are disciples, this is what we want to learn and reflect in our daily lives. It is not easy.

The rich young ruler was enthusiastically faithful to the Law.

Jesus saw this and knew his heart was good, but his earthly attachments were just far too significant:

Mark 10:21-23: (NASB) 21Looking at him, Jesus felt a love for him and said to him, One thing you lack: go and sell all you possess and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me. 22But at these words he was saddened, and he went away grieving, for he was one who owned much property. 23And Jesus, looking around, said to his disciples, How hard it will be for those who are wealthy to enter the kingdom of God!

His attachment to earthly things was too great. Round peg/square hole. The rich young ruler was close but was just not able to let go. This is what discipleship is, and why the gospel feels like it is obsolete. However, it is simply different. This lesson for the Christian is not complicated - it is a simple right-and-wrong scenario: Am I going to live higher or not? Am I going to say, “By God’s grace I get to be the round peg that does not fit in the square hole!” We hope so because we do not want to fit into this world!

Notice Jesus did not say it is impossible for a rich man to enter the kingdom; he said it is difficult. Our hearts must be willing to let go of earthly possessions. If our heart is so positioned, God often will give us stewardship of those possessions to use in His service.

We are not our own. Our things are not ours. We are dedicated to a higher purpose. It is important that as a disciple we realize we are not about an obsolete teaching. We are about a different and higher teaching that does not fit into the context of the environment, but is here for the good of those around us.

On the negative side, this kind of selfless and sacrificial discipleship is completely frowned upon today. Think about how Christianity has been so misrepresented. Think about the unholy leadership that continues to feed such misrepresentation. The narcissistic type of approach from leadership has a direct influence on the followers.

A narcissist’s use of empathy, Narcissism, Dr. Ramani - Because narcissists often just say and do what they want without thinking - that absence of empathy - the problem is that they hurt a lot of people. Because it's not that they have no empathy, they've got some, they know they've done something wrong, and two hours later, six hours later, 24 hours later, five weeks later, may come back to you to say, “Yeah, I can see how that made you upset,” or “I guess I'm sorry I said that.” The apologies are kind of hollow, but they are apologies because they get that they did something wrong. But in the moment their selfish, impulsive need means that they're willing to throw all that empathy stuff out of the window to do what feels right and necessary to them at that moment.

A dear friend of ours and sister in Christ, Micki, who passed away several years ago, is a sad example of this. She had been going to a specific church. That church was all about tithing. She was disabled and on a pathetically low fixed income. She gave and she gave, and the blessings they promised never happened. She would ask why these promised blessings did not happen, and the church leadership would say she had to give more. She gave to the point of not having food, finally leaving the church when she realized this was not the way of the gospel. She could not even feed herself, but the preacher wore $400 shoes. He understood her sincerity in trying to please God and played on it for monetary gain. That is the dark side of all of this. This is why we have to stand for the gospel that is most certainly not obsolete.

2 Peter 2:1-3: (NASB) 1But false prophets also arose among the people, just as there will also be false teachers among you, who will secretly introduce destructive heresies, even denying the Master who bought them, bringing swift destruction upon themselves. 2Many will follow their sensuality, and because of them the way of the truth will be maligned; 3and in their greed they will exploit you with false words; their judgment from long ago is not idle, and their destruction is not asleep.

The Apostle Peter is specific here about what happened in his day, and it is scary. False prophets…arose among the people – that is how it was in Israel with a warning applicable to our day within the Christian community.

These false teachers lead the people in sensual (immoral) doings – luring some to “follow me.” This is NOT what the gospel is. This is a corrupted form of the gospel being taught today.

The real gospel is different, higher and selfless. Discipleship has a high moral standard that represents teachings of Jesus accurately, not for personal gain and power. Although darkness and evil surrounds us, it is not an excuse to let up. We have to stand for something higher.

Contrary to the way this Christian-in-name-only approach teaches, we are given clear and concise direction:

Romans 12:1-2: (NASB) 1Therefore I urge you, brethren, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies a living and holy sacrifice, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service of worship. 2And do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what the will of God is, that which is good and acceptable and perfect.

That which is good and acceptable and perfect - walking in the footsteps of Jesus, doing what he did and treating others the way he did. Living in the 21st century does not change God’s applicable high standard.

We are to have the same humility, the same selflessness, the same true empathy on both sides of the issue, so we can actually stand for the people and not make it all about ME.

Be transformed by the renewing of your mind… This spiritual transformation is for the purpose of living your discipleship in an unfriendly world – that is what we are facing:

1 Peter 1:13-16: (NASB) 13Therefore, prepare your minds for action, keep sober in spirit, fix your hope completely on the grace to be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ. 14As obedient children, do not be conformed to the former lusts which were yours in your ignorance, 15but like the Holy One who called you, be holy yourselves also in all your behavior; 16because it is written, You shall be holy, for I am holy.

Peter understood how difficult it is to stand out in a crowd for a holy purpose. Do not be conformed to the former lusts…be holy for I am holy – this does not mean we will not make mistakes and revert back to old habits. It is how quickly we recover and realize our mistakes and move forward in our discipleship. This is not saying we have to be perfect. We just need to have the right heart intent and desire to be the disciple God wants us to be. It is a struggle and not always easy. Remember the importance of humility.

Keep getting up and fix what needs to be fixed. Do not allow the gospel to become obsolete.

Discipleship and its necessary suffering are an important process.

It makes us worthy through Christ to be trusted with a glory beyond human comprehension:

Romans 8:14-18: (NASB) 14For all who are being led by the spirit of God, these are sons of God. 15For you have not received a spirit of slavery leading to fear again, but you have received a spirit of adoption as sons by which we cry out, Abba! Father! 16The spirit himself (itself) testifies with our spirit that we are children of God.

Let's really think about this gift. We are adopted into God's spiritual family – this is incredible! We call him Abba, which means Daddy. It is such a privilege to have an intimate relationship with God. 17and if children, heirs also, heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ, if indeed we suffer with him so that we may also be glorified with him. 18For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory that is to be revealed to us. Jesus suffered all that he did and then was given incredible glory. Discipleship says: Follow in the sufferings and let God bless you in His time and His way. We are called to be children of God, fellow heirs with Christ, by way of suffering for a short time, because we are His disciples in a world that does not like it. It does not matter what they like; what matters is what we are called to do.

Be a follower, not the centerpiece. We must eliminate that narcissistic approach inside of all of us. We have to continually tell ourselves to do what Jesus did the best we can.

The gospel and its call to discipleship is all about putting the highest things first and yourself last. Our social media society is all about putting yourself first and then joining in with whatever causes fit into your life. This comparison shows just how lost our world is. True discipleship is a relevant ray of light and hope in a world gone mad.

Our world has gone mad – in fact, it is off the rails! Do we stand for something? What if that “something” does not seem to fit with those around me? So what? If we are following the gospel in a righteous way, as it is written, then it is good it does not fit! It means we are following something higher and better. We do not look down on those around us but need to encourage them to come up higher. Look at the hope in Christ and see the way that can embody a higher standard.

The gospel is not obsolete in this world. It is an important example to follow. But that example will not be there unless each of us decides to make it so by the way we live.

Live the gospel, live as a disciple of Jesus and make a difference! So, is the gospel obsolete?

## Episode 1249 — What Will We Be Doing When We Get to Heaven? (Part II)
Published: 2022-10-03
Episode page: https://christianquestions.com/doctrine/1249-heaven-part-ii/

John 14:3: (NASB) If I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and receive you to myself, that where I am, there you may be also.

Going to heaven is a really big deal. Last week was Part I of our three- part series on what heaven-bound Christians will be doing when they get there. We uncovered the mechanics of why only chosen ones are privileged to go to heaven. We began to scratch the surface regarding what these disciples of Jesus will be doing. It turns out, the job descriptions we focused on were nothing like what most people envision as heavenly life. In this episode, we will dig deeply into what the responsibilities of those heaven bound will be. More than that, we will attempt to understand the “why” of it all by connecting several prophecies and scriptures. Our discoveries will reveal absolutely inspiring details and descriptions of how God’s plan is destined to work!

We encourage you to listen to all three parts in this series while using our companion CQ Rewind Show Notes in order to get the comprehensive answer to this important question.

We only began to answer the question in Part I, so let’s do a quick recap of the basic points we covered to bring us up to speed.

We looked at this topic through the lens of four aspects of the Christian’s heavenly reward:

We left off with this scripture, which is obviously symbolic:

Isaiah 61:3: (NASB) …So they will be called oaks (trees) of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He may be glorified.

As we move on to the next verses, the “work” that these “trees” are called upon to do will unfold:

Isaiah 61:4-5: (NASB) 4Then they will rebuild the ancient ruins, they will raise up the former devastations; and they will repair the ruined cities, the desolations of many generations. 5Strangers will stand and pasture your flocks, and foreigners will be your farmers and your vinedressers.

These trees seem active! They rebuild, raise up and repair – they are working! The trees of righteousness are very stable.

The work mentioned in Isaiah 61 is the work of rebuilding, of bringing order and value back to where all was lost, and as we will soon see, it all will begin with the nation of Israel. As we discuss these next few verses, let’s review a New Testament text we discussed in our last episode - 1 Peter 2:9 - that will help us label the heavenly responsibilities required.

In Part I we addressed the GROUNDWORK the footstep followers of Jesus need to accomplish in order to be prepared for heaven. One of these was to accept the responsibilities and changes that come with discipleship. We have been describing this class of people with some interchangeable terms such as:

These terms describe the same small number of faithful ones who will be in heaven. The goal for all of us here at Christian Questions is to be in this special group.

As if those are not enough titles, let’s read the descriptive verse we will keep returning to:

1 Peter 2:9: (NASB) But you are a chosen <1588> race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession, so that you may proclaim the excellencies of Him who has called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.

Chosen: Strong’s Exhaustive Concordance #1588 eklektos, select; by implication, favorite: - chosen, elect

These verses open major understanding into what heaven will look like. They list several privileges and responsibilities that the faithful disciples of Jesus are not only given now but will be inherited later as well.

While the elements of this 1 Peter scripture are drawn from several Old Testament sources, we see them as all fitting in with the Isaiah 61 description of what the faithful disciples of Jesus will be tasked with once they are given heavenly glory.

Isaiah 61:3-4 shows us these trees of righteousness are a specially chosen group.

Let’s begin by focusing on the element of a chosen race. The King James Version says a chosen generation.

Put in modern terms, the phrase “chosen race” triggers thoughts of racism. Why is that not the case here?

We are talking about God’s representation. This chosen race is a group of people chosen from all nations, races and generations since Jesus lived. There is no racism; it is a chosen group. We cannot put 21st century labels on ancient sacred scriptures.

Revelation 17:14: (NASB) These will wage war against the lamb, and the lamb will overcome them, because he is Lord of lords and King of kings, and those who are with him are the called and chosen <1588> (select) and faithful.

This word for chosen is only used in the New Testament to describe Jesus and his true disciples.

The phrase “chosen people” reminds us historically of the nation of Israel:

Deuteronomy 7:6: (KJV) For thou art an holy people unto the LORD thy God; the LORD thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto Himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.

Israel has always been God’s chosen people. Israel ultimately retains favor with God as the blesser nation on earth in the kingdom (the sand of the seashore in the promise to Abraham we will review shortly). The true disciples

of Jesus made up from all nations (the stars of heaven in that same promise) are the chosen and faithful described in Revelation 17:14.

1 Peter 2:9 calls these special ones a chosen race.

But chosen for what? That is our core question – what will they be doing from heaven?

In part, they will be rebuilding the broken earth and blessing resurrected humanity.

Remember the promise given to Abraham:

Genesis 22:17-18: (NASB) 17indeed I will greatly bless you, and I will greatly multiply your seed as the stars of the heavens and as the sand which is on the seashore… 18In your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed, because you have obeyed My voice.

We have talked about this incredible promise given to Abraham many times on Christian Questions. Every time we read it we are impressed by how it explains the breadth of God’s plan. Your seed as the stars of the heavens - does this not sound like something spiritual? And as the sand which is on the seashore – earthly. In your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed, because Abraham was obedient. Putting this together, we have the promise of the trees of righteousness playing a very important role as this spiritual seed. We see its fulfillment here:

Galatians 3:16: (NASB) Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. He does not say, and to seeds, as referring to many, but rather to one, and to your seed, that is, Christ.

Galatians 3:29: (NASB) And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's descendants, heirs according to promise.

Heirs according to the promise - meaning the promise that in your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed. And here Galatians says those who belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's descendants - the chosen race - are part of that seed of blessing. What a privilege!

But the inheritance the faithful ones are given is a huge mess. Taking Adam’s sinful race of billions and billions and then transforming them into God's kingdom of righteousness on earth is an enormous undertaking.

In a sense, it is like the devastating pathway of the recent hurricanes we just experienced full of pain and heartache. On September 28, 2022, Hurricane Ian slammed into the west coast of Florida, and then other states, causing death and billions of dollars of destruction. More than two million people lost power and some also lost water - my wife and I included. We have a “boil water mandate” in our town. Repairing all that damage the hurricane caused will take years, if not decades. The mental health and stress of the people directly affected might never be repaired in this lifetime. But in the kingdom on earth, the faithful ones are given the privilege of helping to rebuild. What a merciful plan of salvation our heavenly Father had in place right from the start.

The work that has to be done to reconstruct peoples’ lives from a hurricane is a great microcosm example of what will need to be done in the kingdom. The Bible assures us the majority of the billions and billions of people who ever lived will be resurrected back on earth. Think of the joy of children who died coming back to their parents, families finding each other and seeing their loved ones again. There are logistics involved on how, when and where everyone will be raised, housed, fed and educated on what has happened and what their future looks like. There will be a lot of work!

The Bible does not give the details of how this will be accomplished, but we know that to make the “blessing of all the families of the earth” prophecy come true, it will take a lot of work. It will be amazing - miracles by the minute! We cannot wait to see it happen. And we know the trees of righteousness are behind all this according to this prophecy.

Let’s look through Lens 4 of heavenly responsibilities again as it relates to the chosen race:

This major task requires God’s power through Jesus and these chosen ones. Further scriptural clarity on the restitution work to come:

Acts 3:20-21: (KJV) 20And he shall send Jesus Christ, which before was preached unto you: 21Whom the heaven must receive until the times of restitution of all things, which God hath spoken by the mouth of all his holy prophets since the world began.

Times of restitution – the time for restoration, rebuilding and restoring. The Isaiah prophecy shows these trees of righteousness to be a chosen race; chosen to rebuild and bless. They are put into a position of primary responsibility under Christ to get all this work done.

Let’s go to this next prophecy in Ezekiel. God says He will “cause” things to happen, and we can now see that Jesus and his true disciples will “make” these things happen. God “causes” and then He has others to get the job done. Before we review this, we note how some feel the literal fulfillment of this prophecy already happened when Israel became a nation in 1948.

How do we know it has a secondary fulfillment in the future kingdom?

The context tells us the primary fulfillment is in the future kingdom.

First notice God's approach and then how the nations around Israel acknowledge the LORD - this is yet future:

Ezekiel 36:33-36: (NASB) 33Thus says the Lord GOD, On the day that I cleanse you from all your iniquities, I will cause the cities to be inhabited, and the waste places will be rebuilt. 34The desolate land will be cultivated instead of being a desolation in the sight of everyone who passes by. 35They will say, this desolate land has become like the garden of Eden; and the waste, desolate and ruined cities are fortified and inhabited. 36Then the nations that are left round about you will know that I, the LORD, have rebuilt the ruined places and planted that which was desolate; I, the LORD, have spoken and will do it.

What a picture of what is to come! First, God will forgive the iniquities of the people. Second, the land will be cleaned up and then cultivated. Third, cities will be rebuilt. When the garden of Eden is mentioned it does not mean we will be sitting in our own perfect gardens. It is a picture of perfection, and work will be done to bring it to that point. The land becoming again like the garden of Eden does not mean an absence of technology and everybody gets to name a lion!

On the day that I cleanse you from all your iniquities - it will be a future work. The nation of Israel will be cleansed, and it ends with - the nations that are left round about you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken and will do it. We have not seen this yet, which is why we know this is a future event. These prophecies all work together! The trees of righteousness will be the heavenly representatives driving all this work.

From Heavenly Groundwork to Heavenly Beings: Jesus’ true disciples are chosen for a reason. They will be an integral part of the massive restoration work that planet earth and its people will need. They will represent and accomplish the works and plan of God as strong and immovable symbols of righteousness. No wonder the groundwork they need to accomplish in this life is so demanding!

Understanding and appreciating the symbolism of biblical prophecy really expands our comprehension of God’s amazing plan!

The disciples of Jesus are a “chosen race” that will deliver restitution. What other heavenly responsibilities will they have?

As we will see the heavenly responsibilities pile up, we will also notice that these responsibilities will be primarily focused on earthly restoration. This may sound odd; they go to heaven so they can do all this work on earth? Why? They go to heaven to be given the power and authority to accomplish the greatest restoration work in earth’s history! Once they receive this power, God releases them to begin this restoration.

Continuing:

Isaiah 61:6: (NASB) But you will be called the priests of the LORD; you will be spoken of as ministers of our God… These two designations need to be individually understood. First, we will focus on priests of the LORD. We are NOT talking about priests like in some Christian denominations today.
